data.narrative:
Lyten, a Series C frontier-energy company, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private companies and 1 public peer in the Climate & Energy sector. The company has raised $1.33B to date.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression methodology uses the $1.3B total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implying a $2.3B valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-stage, same-sector comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—yields a $1.0B median valuation, with a full range spanning $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $850M (low) to $2.6B (high), with a median of $1.6B. The 1.7x spread between low and high reflects material uncertainty around the appropriate comparable set weighting and stage-transition multiples in a heterogeneous frontier-tech sector. Key sensitivities include whether later-stage funding announcements among peers signal further revaluation and the degree to which Lyten's specific technology roadmap and capital efficiency align with the faster-scaling comparables (KoBold) versus the more conservative peers (Amogy).
